what_happened: Apple announced it had acquired Emagic, the German maker of the Logic professional music production software, which became a wholly owned division. Emagic's Windows product line was discontinued on 30 September 2002, moving Logic to the Macintosh alone.
why_it_matters: It moved a professional creative application in-house and ended its cross-platform availability, the line of work that later produced GarageBand and Logic Pro. It is a platform-consolidation event rather than an internet one.
caution: Six days before the node date, so it is a proximity match, not a same-day one, and the press release is a US-dated corporate announcement against a UTC node timestamp. The developmental fit is weak and should not be talked up: this node sits in the chapter 'The Internet becomes a shared Web', about standards, linking and shared information environments, and an acquisition of music-production software is not that. Recorded because it is firmly dated and primary-sourced, not because it fits.

event_title: US-CERT advises abandoning Internet Explorer after the Download.Ject attack
what_happened: After the Download.Ject (Scob) attack, in which compromised IIS servers silently installed a backdoor and keylogger on the machines of people merely viewing a web page, US-CERT took the unusual step of advising users to browse with something other than Internet Explorer, citing flaws in its zone security model, DHTML object model, MIME-type determination and ActiveX.
why_it_matters: A national CERT telling the public to stop using the dominant browser made browser choice a security decision rather than a preference, and is commonly cited as part of what opened the ground for Firefox.
caution: This is the date the advice was reported, not necessarily the date CERT issued it; the underlying vulnerability note is the primary record and I have not read it directly. The attack itself ran roughly 21-25 June, so the episode straddles the node date rather than landing on it. Fit to the chapter is partial: it belongs squarely to 'privacy and control become design problems', but not to the 'social, mobile and cloud' half of the same chapter heading.

what_happened: Cloudflare announced it was terminating 8chan as a customer, effective midnight Pacific that night, after the site's role in inspiring mass violence. The post is timestamped 2019-08-05T01:44:16Z.
why_it_matters: An infrastructure provider, not a platform, decided what could remain reachable on the web, and said so publicly. It became a reference point for how far down the stack content decisions can be pushed.
caution: The date match is exact in UTC and the source is the company's own dated post, so the dating is as strong as it gets. The developmental fit is the weak part, and the strength of the date should not be allowed to carry it: this node sits in the chapter 'Perception becomes a developer platform', about machine senses being made available as reusable components, and an infrastructure provider withdrawing service from a website is not that. Exactly the case the ledger's own method warns about, where a date match is exact while its interpretation is weak.

event_title: Apple suspends the Siri grading programme
what_happened: Apple suspended worldwide the practice of having contractors listen to and grade snippets of Siri recordings, after a Guardian report from a former grader described routinely hearing confidential material. Apple said it would review the programme and later let users opt in.
why_it_matters: The human review behind machine perception became visible, and a vendor suspended a production quality-control pipeline over it. Google paused its Assistant reviews in the same period and Microsoft's Skype and Cortana review was reported days later.
caution: Three days before the node date, and it is secondary reporting of a statement Apple gave to press rather than a dated Apple release, so the day is the reporting day. Unlike the Cloudflare item this one does fit the chapter closely: speech perception offered as a platform feature, and the human labour underneath it. The pairing is worth noticing rather than hiding, since the item that fits the chapter is not the item that matches the date.
